explanation: Okapis and giraffes are the only living members of the giraffe family. Male okapis even have short, skin-covered horns, and both strip leaves with long, flexible tongues.

claims.text: The okapi belongs to the giraffe family, Giraffidae.
Zebras, antelopes and tapirs belong to other families (the horse family, the cattle and antelope family, and the tapir family), not the giraffe family.
The okapi and the giraffe are the only living members of the giraffe family, Giraffidae.
Male okapis have short, skin-covered horns (ossicones), like those of giraffes.
Okapis and giraffes use long, flexible tongues to strip leaves.

By genus the giraffe family has two living members, Okapia and Giraffa. By species it has two only if every giraffe belongs to one species, and several authorities now treat the giraffe as four species.
